QuestionStmt.S: Find $\Delta n$ when 1 mol of each NH$_3$(g) and HCl$(g)$, reacts to form solid NH$_4$Cl.

Solution.S:
The reaction is:

$$\mathrm{NH_3(g) + HCl(g) \rightarrow NH_4Cl(s)}$$

For $\Delta n$, we consider only gaseous moles:

$$\Delta n = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$$

Here, the product NH$_4$Cl is solid, so gaseous product moles = 0.

Gaseous reactants are: $1$ mol NH$_3$ + $1$ mol HCl = $2$ mol.

So,

$$\Delta n = 0 - 2 = -2$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{-2}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
